### Architect · Answer

Event: `ef3b22483f1afdf3c05c4637849a1e60` · 2026-10-03T04:50:49Z

> Node B7 written (todo, M1, Tier B, S, no needs). Brief with exact page lines: .wash/local/B7-implementer.md.
> 
> What the code shows: the bench runs cases one at a time, so the race needs two bench processes in one worktree. Examples: a single-case loop beside a whole run, or a sweep beside a bench. prepare() packs target/<triple>/<profile>/redoubt-kernel, the same path for every feature set. Cargo's lock serialises builds, but another run's build can overwrite that file between this build and this pack. Bundles, logs, disks and corrupted ELFs also go to fixed paths under target/testbench/. The implementer reproduces it first: a whole bench plus a handle-chain-fault loop.
> 
> Fix: isolate, do not lock. A run-wide lock would queue every agent's one-case check behind a 30-minute bench.
> - Pack the executable that cargo's --message-format=json reports for this build (deps/redoubt_kernel-<hash>, hashed per feature set), copied into the run's own directory in the same build call. The same goes for the loader and programs.
> - Every file a run writes goes under target/testbench/run-<pid>/, with target/testbench/last pointing at the latest run.
> 
> Keepers: host tests showing interleaved feature builds each pack their own bytes, and two runs that share no file. A deterministic self-check if one can be written, else said so. 20 overlapped reproductions after the fix with no failure.
> 
> Pages: testbench.md "How to use it" (per-run directories; runs may overlap) and GATE1-free GETTING-STARTED.md line 85 (target/testbench/last/).
> 
> B6: keep it separate; no need to ask the owner about merging. B7 is a correctness fix that should not wait on the owner's decision. Its per-run directory and artifact copies are what B6's --jobs needs anyway, so B6, if cut, needs B7 and gets smaller: --seeds and --jobs only.

### Orchestrator · Progress

Event: `be0681aa68b086b07b72df0eb799eeb4` · 2026-10-03T05:13:53Z

> B7's checkpoint reproduced the race hard: a whole bench beside a handle-chain-fault loop gave 13 of 282 cases a wrong kernel (8 the loop's fault kernel, 5 a checked kernel missing their own feature) and the loop 7 wrong packs in 559. Two facts corrected from the brief, which I approved as implementation: cargo's JSON `executable` is the uplifted unhashed path, so the fix is a per-run --target-dir with CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR pointing at the shared target/ (cache shared, uplift per run under cargo's own lock); and run-<pid> collides because each in-dev call is its own pid namespace, so the run dir is run-<pid>-<start ns> with a flock for its life. The page line becomes run-<pid>-<time>/; say if you want it otherwise.
